whyos.summary: Type a sum, get the answer: functions, hex and binary
whyos.description:
Type a sum on the keyboard; its result shows as you type, and Enter (or =)
works it out and puts it on the roll above. Up and Down bring earlier sums
back to change them. Starting with + * / ^ % or ! goes on from the last
answer, and an x after a number means times.

It knows + - * / ^, brackets, n% (n/100), n! and mod; pi, e and ans
(the last answer); sqrt, cbrt, abs, exp, ln, log, log2, sin, cos, tan,
asin, acos, atan, sinh, cosh, tanh, round, floor and ceil. 2pi and
3(4+5) multiply. Numbers can be written as 0xff, 0b1010 or 1.5e3, and a
whole-number answer also shows in hexadecimal and binary.

Angles are in degrees; Tab switches to radians, as the setting (the clover
key) does, and the choice is kept. The circle key shows the sums worked
out, the diamond the keys. Esc clears the line, and on an empty line
closes the calculator, as the logo key does.
whyos.changelog: The SDK's fix of WhyOS ca53300: keys that come before a new screen's first frame (a quick press right after the one that opened it) are no longer lost.
